summary: John's great-grandmother (mother of his paternal grandfather James C. Meier); daughter of Addison F. Pringle and Catherine E. Heffernan, the link that joins the Meier line to the Pringle, Heffernan, Lamoreaux and colonial lines.
bio: Florence Louise Pringle was born in Plymouth, Luzerne County, about 1903-04 (the tree says 1903; the 1910 census age of 6 suggests 1904; she was 22 in April 1926, 25 in April 1930 and 45 in April 1950). She was one of eight known children of Addison F. Pringle and Catherine E. (Heffernan) Pringle; her siblings were Genevieve (1893), Joseph Vincent (1895), Mary E. (1898), Anna Theresa (1901), Helen (1906), Francis (1909) and Catherine (1912). In 1910 the family was enumerated at Larksville (FamilySearch residence events; Round 2 cites the same 1910 census as 'Plymouth'), where the McGuire family of her future daughter-in-law also lived. By 1926 she was a clerk living with her parents at 28 Huston St, Wilkes-Barre. On 16 Apr 1926 she and William F. Meier, a clerk born at Tamaqua, of 16 Barney St, swore a marriage-licence application (No. 10768); they were married on 20 Apr 1926 by Rev. D. W. McCarthy at Wilkes-Barre. In 1930 she, William and sons William (about 3) and James (1 9/12) lived at 55 Cedar Street, Wilkes-Barre, on the same census sheet as her parents at 28 Huston St. In 1943 her father's obituary listed her as 'Mrs. William Meier, Wilkes-Barre'. In 1950 the household at house 55 was William F. (45, supervisor at a coal company), Florence (45), William Jr. (23), James C. (21) and Barbara Ann (14). William died at Wilkes-Barre on 4 Jul 1963. Florence died in 1980 (tree); her death record was not checked because the online PA death index ends in 1966. A funeral notice for an infant 'Florence Irene Meier' from Wilkes-Barre, published 11 Oct 1933, may be a daughter (speculative; not in the 1933 PA death index).
funFacts: In 1910 the Pringles and the McGuires (family of her future daughter-in-law Kathryn McGuire) both lived in small-town Larksville, 18 years before their children married.
In 1930 she lived on the same census sheet as her parents: Meiers at 55 Cedar St, Pringles at 28 Huston St.
Both she and her husband were clerks when they married: a white-collar generation, one step up from her uncle Orange Pringle, a slate picker at 13 in 1880.
